pages.name: Primary logo
pages.title: The paper’s own lettering.
pages.subtitle: OVER THE EDGE over the line UNBC’S STUDENT NEWSPAPER, exactly as the website draws it. It is never redrawn or reset in a font.

elements.text: UNBC’s independent student newspaper, in print and at overtheedge.unbc.ca. Breaking news, vibrant clubs, can’t-miss events, and a shared university calendar.
The site’s header sets the subtext in ink (#262626) under forest words. That two-colour original is in logos/source/. Every other logo in this kit is one colour.

pages.name: Logo family
pages.title: Four ways to sign.
pages.subtitle: Choose the one that fits the space. Keep it in one colour, and keep the O whole.

elements.text: The O is the logo’s own first letter. Use it alone only where the name cannot be read: favicons, app icons, avatars, patterns.

pages.name: Clear space and sizes
pages.title: Room to breathe.
pages.subtitle: Half the height of the O, clear on every side. Below 288 px wide, drop the subtext.

elements.text: The subtext’s capitals are 6 px tall at 288 px wide on screen, and 1.2 mm tall at 58 mm in print. Below either, use the logo without subtext; below that, the O.

pages.name: Colour
pages.title: Forest on newsprint.
pages.subtitle: One green, one paper, one ink. The rest supports them, and red is only ever an editor’s mark.

elements.text: Lichen #E3EFCF · Sage #6AA380 · Moss #466855 · Kraft #D4C8AA · Pulp #DBD0BA · Bark #7D6B56 · Proof #B54A35 · White #FFFFFF.

Text pairs, measured: ink on newsprint 13.4 : 1 · forest on newsprint 8.1 : 1 · white on forest 9.1 : 1 · lichen on forest 7.6 : 1 · white on pine 12.7 : 1 · lichen on pine 10.6 : 1 · white on moss 6.2 : 1 · ink on sage 5.2 : 1 · bark on newsprint 4.53 : 1 · proof on newsprint 4.7 : 1 · white on proof 5.3 : 1. At 24 px and up only: sage on pine 4.3 : 1 · sage on forest 3.1 : 1. Proof is for Breaking and Correction only.

pages.subtitle: Serif for the news, Anton for the front page, Inter for the interface, Plex Mono for the dateline, one hand-written note.

pages.name: Motion
pages.title: Off the press, one word at a time.
pages.subtitle: The logo prints in word by word, then holds. Rules roll, pages turn, and the O fills while you wait.

rows: Ease out, the site’s own curve

elements.text: Print, don’t perform. The logo arrives word by word and then holds. It never bounces, spins, blurs, glows or changes colour, and every logo study ends on the exact still logo.
One thing at a time. Stagger related parts by 80 ms, left to right and top to bottom, the order a reader takes in a page.
Loops are for waiting. Only loaders loop, and only the O or a print device loops, never the full logo. Stop the loop as soon as the wait is over.
Still is a valid frame. With reduced motion, show the final frame. Nothing should depend on the animation to be understood.
All the studies, with replay, are in motion/index.html in the kit and in brandkit’s Motion tab.

pages.name: Files
pages.title: Use the right file for the job.
pages.subtitle: The same artwork drives the vectors, images, templates and web components.

rows: Transparent artwork for slides and documents.
Inline colour inheritance and local fonts.
One source for the whole identity.

elements.text: Full logo width, screen and print. Without subtext: 96 px / 20 mm.
Height of the O on its own.
Open index.html in the kit to browse every file. Edit brand.json, or this brand’s script, and rebuild to change any of them.
Over the Edge / ADDITIONAL SUPPORTING STUDIES
Additional supporting studies. Existing identifying artwork and identity guidance remain unchanged.
Use one pattern family per surface. Small repeats give texture; larger fields suit covers and displays. Keep small text and the complete identifying logo on a clear ground.

studies.name: Press
studies.use: Site intro, video opener, issue launch
studies.description: OVER, THE and EDGE print in one at a time, dropping a few pixels into place; then UNBC’S STUDENT NEWSPAPER rises under them.

studies.name: Stack
studies.description: The stacked logo, each line rising out of its own mask, as on the October 2025 cover.

studies.name: Ink
studies.use: Longer moments: video, keynote, a new volume
studies.description: The logo is uncovered left to right, the way a roller lays ink on a plate.

studies.name: Rolling rules
studies.use: Lists and search results while they load
studies.description: The issue index’s dashed rules roll past, one line after another.

studies.name: Page count
studies.description: Anton page numbers turn over: 03, 05, 10, as in the index.

studies.name: O fill
studies.use: Page and app loading, 24 px and up
studies.description: The O fills with forest from the foot up, holds, and empties. The O only; it stops when loading ends.

studies.name: Paper airplane
studies.use: Sending a tip, submitting a story
studies.description: A paper airplane, like the one drawn on the October 2025 cover, glides along a dashed line.

studies.name: Headline
studies.use: Article headers, hero headlines, title slides
studies.description: Each line of a Source Serif headline rises out of its own mask.

studies.name: Card pick
studies.description: A story card lifts 3 px, shifts 1 px and turns 0.4°, like a clipping picked up off the desk, then settles.

studies.name: Index
studies.use: The issue index, tables of contents
studies.description: Each dashed rule draws across, then its page number and headline come in.

studies.name: Chip
studies.description: A filter chip presses in to 96%, and its border and label turn forest.

studies.name: Turn page
studies.description: The next page slides over from the right edge, square-cornered, like turning a broadsheet.

studies.name: Skeleton
studies.use: Cards and lists before content arrives
studies.description: Placeholder lines in Pulp with a Newsprint highlight passing along them.

patternCollection.description: The original O becomes a printed texture, while column rules, halftone dots, torn paper and registration marks draw on the newspaper’s production language. These supporting studies extend the Forest press palette without replacing the masthead.
